title: Quantization Deprecation & Grandfathering Policy
author: Maya Patel
content:
Summary
This page documents Redwood Inference's policy for deprecating quantized model artifacts and the associated grandfathering and migration paths teams must follow. The goal is to balance operational safety and customer continuity: retire unsupported/unsafe quant profiles while minimizing user impact and enabling automated migration.

Scope
- Applies to: quantized model release artifacts (quant profiles and deployment metadata), automated quant fallback policies, and any mixed-precision runtime configurations used by Redwood-hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments.
- Excludes: ephemeral experiment artifacts in personal forks and internal research-only branches.

Principles
1) Safety-first: Any quant profile that causes measurable coherence degradation, hallucination increase, or failure-class regressions must be remediated or deprecated.
2) Predictability: Teams must provide clear timelines, compatibility guarantees, and rollback paths.
3) Minimizing customer disruption: Grandfathering tiers and automated compatibility shims should be used where feasible.
4) Observability: Deprecation decisions require telemetry justification, a triage trail, and post-deprecation monitoring.

Definitions
- Quant profile: metadata and parameters describing a quantization configuration (bit-widths, per-channel vs per-tensor, calibration tables) for a particular model family and service.
- Deprecation event: formal decision to stop recommending or supporting a quant profile for production traffic.
- Grandfathering: a temporary compatibility commitment for customers using a deprecated profile (soft or hard grandfathering explained below).

Deprecation Criteria
A quant profile should be considered for deprecation if any of the following conditions are met: 
- Reproducible fidelity regression: end-to-end eval delta exceeds the service's fidelity budget (see Acceptance Criteria section).
- Safety regression: new profile causes a measurable increase in safety sentinel failures or content policy infractions.
- Runtime instability: excessive OOMs, cache corruption, or KV-cache miss amplification tied to the quant kernel.
- Infeasible maintenance: underlying dependency (hardware/driver) reaches EOL or cannot be patched.

Decision Workflow (numbered procedure)
1. Detection: Alert triggered by eval pipeline, shadow traffic, or customer report. Capture sample set, seed, and telemetry.
2. Triage: Run localized probes (steps A–D below) and produce a triage ticket in the regression tracker.
3. Review: Quantization council (or delegated owners) assess failure modes and propose either remediation, rollback, or deprecation.
4. Announcement: If deprecation is chosen, publish the timeline and migration plan to affected stakeholders and affected customers.
5. Execution: Implement automated router shims, migration hooks, and monitoring.
6. Post-deprecation monitoring: Track regression KPI for 30/90/180 days depending on severity.

Triage probes (A–D)
A) Shadow re-run: Replay failing requests with both quant and baseline fp16/fp32 to measure delta.
B) Probe amplification: Run adversarial/fuzz probes focused on slices that failed in the field.
C) Model attribution: Check weight-sensitivity maps and quantization-sensitivity heatmaps.
D) Runtime reproduction: Simulate production batch and KV-cache behavior to surface instability.

Grandfathering levels and timelines
- Soft Grandfathering (90 days): Deprecated profile remains usable but will not receive new optimizations. Customers are notified; automatic migration is scheduled with opt-out.
- Hard Grandfathering (30 days): Deprecated profile remains accessible with reduced SLAs and a strong recommendation to migrate. After 30 days, traffic is migrated unless exemption is granted.
- Immediate Removal: For critical safety/runtime failures where continuing to serve would harm customers or infra, the profile can be pulled with emergency notification and a short remediation window (typically 48 hours).

Communication and Customer Impact Minimization
- Publish deprecation notices in the Console (model and quant profile pages), API changelogs, and the status page.
- Provide a migration guide and an automated converter where possible.
- Offer a temporary compatibility shim that translates older quant metadata into the new runtime path for up to the grandfathering window.

Migration Patterns and Recipes
1) Automatic conversion (preferred): Use quant-convert tool to map old per-channel scales to the new quant manifest. Steps: 
   - CLI: redwood-quant convert --input old-profile.json --output converted-profile.json --check-stability
   - Validation: run `redwood-eval-run --profile converted-profile.json --slices critical` and compare SLI deltas.
2) Shadow canary: route 2–5% of traffic to converted profile for 7 days, monitor fidelity, latency, and error budgets.
3) Manual pinning: for customers unable to accept migration, open an exception and schedule a migration with solutions-engineering.

Acceptance criteria to prevent deprecation false positives
- Fidelity: aggregated delta across service-critical slices must exceed the fidelity budget for two independent seeds and be reproducible in shadow re-run.
- Latency/Cost: conversion should not increase p95 latency by >5% or token cost by >7% without explicit approval.
- Safety: safety sentinel delta must show statistically significant regression (p < 0.01) on core sentinels.

Rollback and Emergency Recovery
- Rollback via routing: route traffic back to baseline model variant using the runtime rollout API. Example: 
  curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/rollouts/revert 
  -d '{"service":"chat-frontend","route":"/v1/generate","target_variant":"baseline-fp16"}' 
- Artifact rollback: restore artifact from quant-artifacts-backup S3 bucket using the proven timestamp.
- Communication: page owners and affected customers via email and status page.

Operational Requirements (table represented as lines)
- Ownership: Each quant profile must list an owner_team and a single oncall owner.
- Telemetry: Must include slice-metrics, seed-hash, kernel-trace, and runtime OOM counters.
- Backups: Quant artifacts retained for 180 days; critical production artifacts retained for 540 days.
- Checkpoints: Every production quant promotion must include a stability-checkpoint tag (e.g., stable-2026-02-01).

Example quant manifest (JSON example)
- fields: model_family, profile_version, bitwidth_map, calibration_hash, runtime_hint
- sample: {"model_family":"redwood-13b","profile_version":"qv1.9","bitwidth_map":"per_channel:8,kv:16","calibration_hash":"abc1234","runtime_hint":"prefer-fast-kernel"}

Runbook: executing a deprecation (short checklist)
1) Create deprecation ticket with triage artifacts and link shadow probe results.
2) Produce stakeholder announcement and customer impact list.
3) Schedule automated conversion job and create canary.
4) Validate canary for 7 days, then initiate migration or enable grandfathering exemption.
5) Close ticket after post-deprecation monitoring window.

Monitoring and KPIs
- Track: fidelity-delta, safety-sentinel-rate, p95-latency, runtime-oom-rate, quant-fallback-rate.
- Targets: fidelity-delta within service budget after migration; fallback-rate < 0.5% for 30 days post-migration.

Ownership, Escalation and SLA
- Owner: Quant Platform (team alias: quant-platform@redwood.ai) owns policy enforcement.
- Escalation: if rollback not possible within 8 hours for P1 incidents, escalate to SRE and Product Security.
- Customer SLA: during grandfathering, provide a documented SLA downgrade if applicable and list remediation timeline.

Frequently Asked Questions (FAQ)
Q: Can customers request permanent pinning of a deprecated profile?
A: Permanent pinning is discouraged. Exceptions require security review and an explicit operational contract with cost and risk acceptance.

Q: How are black-box third-party kernels handled?
A: If a third-party kernel is the source of instability, we will attempt to shim or isolate it; if not feasible the profile will be scheduled for deprecation with emergency mitigations where necessary.

Related references
- Shadow cohort and rollback playbook (internal): /applied-ml-and-evals/quantization-profiles/quant-shadow-cohort-strategy-and-rollback-playbook-2026
- Onboarding playbook for quant migrations: /applied-ml-and-evals/model-onboarding/onboarding-to-service-eval-playbook-for-cost-latency-quality-triage-2026

Appendix: Communication templates (short)
- Notice to customers: 
  Subject: Action required: Deprecation of quant profile qv1.9 for redwood-13b
  Body: We have scheduled the deprecation of qv1.9 for redwood-13b on YYYY-MM-DD. You will be migrated to qv2.0 unless you opt out by YYYY-MM-DD. See migration guide: <link>. Contact solutions-eng@redwood.ai for exceptions.

- Internal incident template: include triage ticket id, failing slices, shadow delta snapshot, and recommended mitigation (rollback/conversion).

Document maintenance
- Review cadence: this policy is reviewed annually by the Quant Platform team or immediately after any major safety incident.
- Owner contact: quant-platform@redwood.ai
